components.css: .ds-mark { font-family: var(--serif); font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-amp { font-style: italic; color: var(--gold); letter-spacing: 0.02em; margin: 0 0.04em; } .ds-tile { position: relative; display: grid; max-width: 420px; padding: clamp(24px, 3vw, 36px); background: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 0; color: var(--espresso); text-decoration: none; transition: border-color 0.25s, box-shadow 0.3s, transform 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-tile .ds-mark { font-size: clamp(1.5rem, 2.4vw, 2.125rem); } .ds-tile::before { content: ""; position: absolute; left: -1px; right: -1px; top: -1px; height: 3px; background: var(--gold); transform: scaleX(0); transform-origin: left; transition: transform 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-tile:hover { border-color: var(--espresso); box-shadow: 0 18px 36px -24px rgba(44, 35, 28, 0.45); transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-tile:hover::before, .ds-tile:focus-visible::before { transform: scaleX(1); } .ds-tile:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--espresso); outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-tile-name { margin-top: 14px; font: 600 1.125rem/1.3 var(--sans); } .ds-tile-text { margin-top: 8px; font: 400 1rem/1.5 var(--sans); color: #4a3b2f; } .ds-tile-go { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; margin-top: 24px; padding-top: 18px; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule-soft); font: 600 0.9375rem/1 var(--sans); letter-spacing: 0.06em; } .ds-tile-go svg { width: 1.1em; height: 1.1em; transition: transform 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-tile:hover .ds-tile-go svg { transform: translateX(4px); }

narrative.overview:
The site is a printed calling card for a group of four divisions, composed entirely from the FLEET&FLOAT identity sheet. Every name is set the way the logo sets it: Bodoni Moda capitals spaced wide, with an italic gold ampersand between the two Fs. Espresso and gold come straight from the logo files. A espresso band opens every page with the white mark and the sygnet (white ring, gold inner ring, gold ampersand). Below it the ground turns pale and cool, and content sits on white sheets edged with a thin espresso rule.

Density is calm and orderly, like good stationery. Sections are separated by a generous fluid step and by hairline rules, not by colour blocks. Each division is a white tile carrying its own mark, a one-line description and a espresso line drawing of what it offers (vehicles, a screen, a houseboat, an office). Depth stays quiet: corners are square, surfaces sit flat at rest, and lift appears only when a tile is approached or a raster screenshot needs to read as an object.

The brand assets are binding: the logo and sygnet are used as supplied and never redrawn or recoloured. The rejected variant of the division tile is the generic one: an icon, a heading and text in a rounded card with a drop shadow.
keyCharacteristics: Names always appear in logo notation: F&F + division in spaced serif capitals with a gold italic ampersand.
A espresso hero band with the white mark and the sygnet opens the home page and every division page; a espresso footer closes them.
Pale cool ground (deep), white sheets, thin espresso rules; square corners everywhere.
Espresso line drawings in one stroke family illustrate each division and are labelled as illustrative.
One signature motion: the tile's gold top line draws in from the left while its arrow slides forward.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: Espresso and gold are the only chromatic colours. Gold marks and underlines; espresso carries everything you read. Gold never sets running text on a light ground.

rules.name: The Ground-Matched Gold Rule
rules.body: Use gold on pale and white grounds and gold-on-dark on espresso bands, exactly as the logo files do. Don't swap them.

rules.name: The Logo Notation Rule
rules.body: The group and division names are always set with the mark component: Bodoni capitals at 0.12–0.14em spacing, with the ampersand in italic gold at 0.02em. Never write "F&F" in the sans, and never set the ampersand roman or in espresso.

rules.name: The Serif Speaks for the Brand Rule
rules.body: Bodoni is reserved for marks, section headlines, nav items, table row heads and the form's division select. Explanation, labels and controls are Barlow.

rules.name: The Lift on Approach Rule
rules.body: Tiles rest flat with a thin rule border. Only hover or focus brings the espresso border, the lift, and the gold top line.

rules.name: The Square Sheet Rule
rules.body: No border-radius on any interface surface. The only rounded shapes are inside the supplied app-icon asset and the drawings themselves.

dos: Do set every group and division name with the mark: Bodoni capitals at 0.14em with the italic gold ampersand (gold on light, gold-on-dark on espresso).
Do open each page with the espresso band carrying the white mark and the sygnet, and close it with the espresso footer.
Do separate content with hairlines (rule, rule-soft) and the fluid section step, not with colour blocks or cards.
Do use the double-ring button: espresso on light grounds, light on espresso bands, 52px high, condensed uppercase with the drawn arrow.
Do reserve lift for approach: tiles flat at rest, Tile Lift and the drawn gold top line on hover or focus.
Do mark illustrative drawings as such and show missing facts with the draft marker.
donts: Don't redraw, recolour or re-typeset the logo or the sygnet; use the supplied files and the sygnet component as they are.
Don't round corners on any interface surface.
Don't build division tiles as an icon, heading and text in a rounded card with a drop shadow.
Don't set running text in gold or introduce a third chromatic colour; rust is for errors only.
Don't write "F&F" in the sans or set the ampersand roman.
Don't put shadows on surfaces at rest, except the Proof Frame around a raster screenshot.
